requirement: Describe Healthy Detours as a 12-week randomized two-arm parallel active-control trial in college students comparing the location-tailored Healthy Detours smartphone application with Calorie Counter by FatSecret.

evidence.text: The protocol describes a 12-week RCT of Healthy Detours versus the selected FatSecret control application in college students.

requirement: Define the randomized analysis population, including LSU student status, smartphone and language requirements, consent and identity confirmation, completed baseline surveys and ASA24, and rules for screen failure, withdrawal and loss to follow-up; do not infer unstated eligibility criteria.

evidence.text: The protocol describes online eligibility screening, consent, LSU identity confirmation and baseline surveys but does not enumerate all criteria or define an analysis population.

requirement: Specify the randomization ratio, sequence-generation method, any semester or phone-platform strata or blocks, allocation concealment and the timing after baseline ASA24; the protocol's staff-facing randomization link alone is not a complete allocation specification.

evidence.text: Participants complete the baseline surveys and ASA24 before staff use an individual schedule-page link to reveal assignment, but the algorithm and ratio are not stated.

requirement: Define Healthy Detours as the location-enabled tailored diet, activity and sleep tracking application with tutorial access, and define FatSecret as the publicly available calorie, food and exercise tracking control; preserve the distinction between app-provided data and independently administered outcome instruments.
acceptable_values: app data separate from survey outcomes

evidence.text: The protocol describes selection, installation, registration and tutorial procedures for both applications.

requirement: Use assessments at baseline, 6 weeks and the 12-week post-test, treating 12 weeks as the primary outcome time and 6 weeks as an immediate-change and mediator timepoint; record which measures and app streams are available at each visit.

evidence.text: The protocol schedules baseline enrollment, an emailed six-week survey and a 12-week post-test.
The plan identifies 12-week hypotheses and additional six-week change and mediation analyses.

requirement: Define the primary endpoint as the 12-week Healthy Eating Index derived from ASA24 and compare baseline-adjusted dietary-quality improvement between Healthy Detours and FatSecret.

evidence.text: H1 labels HEI calculated from ASA24 as the primary 12-week dietary-quality outcome and later specifies baseline-adjusted ANCOVA.

requirement: Operationalize ASA24-to-HEI scoring, including dietary recall days, component and total score algorithm, valid-recall criteria, averaging of repeated recalls if any, plausible-intake checks and treatment of incomplete recalls.

evidence.text: The protocol administers ASA24 at baseline but supplies no HEI derivation or validity rules.

requirement: Analyze the prespecified 12-week secondary domains of physical activity using standard IPAQ-SF scoring, sleep using standard PSQI scoring and quality of life using SF-12, while reporting app-entered activity, daily sleep ratings, phone accelerometry and optional wearable data as distinct supporting measures.

evidence.text: H2-H4 name IPAQ-SF, PSQI and SF-12 and separately list app and device-derived activity and sleep measures.

requirement: Predefine scoring and validity rules for IPAQ-SF, PSQI, SF-12, phone accelerometry, Fitbit or other wearable streams, System Usability Scale and URPI, including minimum wear, valid-day, subscale and direction-of-benefit conventions.

evidence.text: The protocol administers four baseline surveys and adds SUS and URPI at post-test but does not give scoring or device-validity rules.

requirement: For each main outcome, present descriptive distributions and an unadjusted simple t-test followed by an ANCOVA of the 12-week outcome with its baseline value as a covariate; do not substitute a change-score-only primary analysis.

evidence.text: The plan calls for descriptive summaries, simple t-tests and ANCOVA adjusted for baseline rather than change from baseline.

requirement: Use Hotelling's T-squared as an omnibus multivariate test of the four outcome response vector and examine within-arm outcome correlation matrices, while distinguishing this omnibus analysis from endpoint-specific ANCOVAs.

evidence.text: The plan proposes simultaneous analysis of four outcomes with Hotelling's T2 and examination of correlations within treatment arms.

requirement: Use a prespecified generalized least-squares repeated-measures model in PROC MIXED as the longitudinal missing-outcome analysis for baseline, 6-week and 12-week data, and define fixed effects, covariance structure, estimation, degrees of freedom, missing-at-random assumption and treatment contrast before implementation.

evidence.text: The plan names generalized least-squares regression in PROC MIXED for dropout between six and twelve weeks but omits model implementation details.

requirement: Report completion and dropout by arm and timepoint and compare baseline and engagement characteristics of completers and dropouts overall and within prespecified subgroups, without treating diagnostic associations as causal evidence about the application.

evidence.text: The plan says dropout characteristics will be intensively examined overall and within subgroups.

requirement: Define the primary treatment-policy estimand using all randomized students analyzed according to assigned application at 12 weeks, with explicit handling of failure to install, app switching, discontinuation, low use, unavailable phone or wearable data and withdrawal; keep utilization-defined effects secondary.

evidence.text: The protocol describes randomization, installation, tracked use and follow-up but no estimand or intercurrent-event strategy.

requirement: Define two-sided alpha, confidence level and multiplicity strategy across the HEI primary endpoint, three secondary domains, endpoint-specific t-tests and ANCOVAs, the Hotelling omnibus test, two post-baseline timepoints and exploratory usage or mediation analyses; otherwise label all nonprimary tests exploratory.

evidence.text: The terse plan proposes multiple outcomes, methods, times, utilization and mediation analyses without alpha, confidence intervals or a complete multiplicity rule.

requirement: Analyze app utilization descriptively using prespecified denominators and metrics such as log-ins, check-ins and EMA likability or satisfaction responses, then define the treatment-received variable, identification assumptions, instrument and covariates for any complier-average causal-effect model.

evidence.text: The plan names usage metrics and a complier-average causal-effect analysis but does not operationalize compliance or identification.

requirement: For mediation, prespecify each 6-week mediator and 12-week outcome, treatment-to-mediator and mediator-to-outcome models, baseline adjustment, temporal ordering, exposure-mediator interaction, bootstrap resampling unit and interval method; treat mediation as exploratory.

evidence.text: The plan proposes six-week mediators for twelve-week outcomes and latest bootstrapping methods without defining variables or models.

requirement: Use the prospective target of 300 college students, approximately 150 enrolled in each of the Fall 2016 and Spring 2017 periods, and distinguish the target from completed or analyzable counts; do not infer equal treatment allocation from semester counts.

evidence.text: The protocol plans 300 students split approximately evenly across two enrollment semesters.

requirement: Account for Fall-versus-Spring enrollment cohort and phone platform in descriptive balance and sensitivity analyses, and confirm whether the target trial is restricted to LSU or includes another campus before adding site effects.

evidence.text: The protocol spans Fall and Spring LSU cohorts and distinct Android and iPhone installation paths but does not specify adjustment or another site.

requirement: State masking by role and timing: enrollment staff reveal assignment to install the application and participants can see application identity, so do not claim participant or site-staff blinding; confirm whether outcome analysts remain masked until the analysis is frozen.

evidence.text: Staff reveal assignment and assist with visibly different application installation and registration workflows.

requirement: Define whether adverse events, privacy incidents, problematic weight-control behavior or device/application harms are collected, identify the exposed safety population and summarize events by assigned app; otherwise document why a formal safety analysis is not applicable.

evidence.text: The protocol collects identifiable registration and tracked application data but contains no safety-analysis procedure.

requirement: Keep the three-page Statistical Analysis Plan annotation-only: the model-visible protocol may expose the two apps, 300 target, baseline, six-week and twelve-week procedures, but must not expose the reference-only HEI hierarchy, ANCOVA, Hotelling T-squared, generalized least squares, CACE or bootstrap-mediation decisions.

evidence.text: Full text and visual review found procedures and timepoints but not the independent plan's executable inferential methods.
The independent plan contains the endpoint hierarchy, ANCOVA, multivariate, missing-data, CACE and mediation decisions.
